claims.text: Homogenized HfNbTaTiZr is single-phase and predominantly BCC at room temperature.
Elevated-temperature deformation of HfNbTaTiZr transitions from dislocation-dominated deformation to enhanced grain-boundary sliding and dynamic recovery.
Dynamic recovery reduces the dislocation density of HfNbTaTiZr at elevated temperatures.
Grain-boundary sliding begins or becomes enhanced in HfNbTaTiZr at elevated temperatures.
Elevated-temperature exposure may produce subtle grain-boundary segregation in HfNbTaTiZr.
Thermal activation facilitates dislocation motion and recovery in HfNbTaTiZr.
Thermally activated dislocation motion and recovery lower the barriers to grain-boundary sliding.
Dynamic recovery and grain-boundary sliding reduce the yield strength of HfNbTaTiZr at elevated temperatures.
Dynamic recovery and grain-boundary sliding reduce the elastic stiffness or elastic modulus of HfNbTaTiZr at elevated temperatures.
The proposed elevated-temperature mechanisms increase the thermal expansion coefficient of HfNbTaTiZr.
Relative to room temperature, the stress-strain response changes from strain hardening to strain softening.
Relative to room temperature, HfNbTaTiZr exhibits a measurable drop in elastic modulus.
Relative to room temperature, HfNbTaTiZr exhibits enhanced and nonlinear thermal expansion.
Below the dynamic-activation threshold, dislocation glide dominates deformation.
Below the dynamic-activation threshold, HfNbTaTiZr has higher yield strength and elastic modulus and a lower thermal expansion coefficient than in the targeted elevated-temperature regime.
The proposed mechanistic transition is expected to occur approximately between 600 and 1000 °C under strain rates typical of high-temperature mechanical testing.
The relevant high-temperature regime approaches approximately 60–80% of the alloy melting temperature.
